citation: Brady, Konkle, Alvarez & Oliva (2008) — Visual long-term memory has a massive storage capacity for object details, PNAS 105(38):14325-14329

source.license: Brady stimulus set is CC-BY for research; v1 port does NOT use the Brady image set to keep the task self-contained without shipping ~30 MB of image assets
source.note: The original Brady et al. 2008 paradigm uses ~2,500 unique object photographs in a study/test recognition design. v1 port reproduces the structural design (study phase + distractor + 2AFC old/new test) using procedurally-generated SVG stimuli (shape × color × pattern × orientation) with 768 unique combinations. The procedural approach (a) ships the entire task in a single experiment.js file, (b) lets us scale stimulus difficulty, and (c) is honest about the simplification (a v2 with the actual Brady photographs will be shipped as a supplementary task).

description: Visual recognition memory in study/test format. Study phase: 50 unique procedurally-generated stimuli, 2.5s each. Distractor: 30s arithmetic. Test phase: 100 trials (50 'old' + 50 'new' lures), 2AFC old/new judgment with 4s deadline.
